Some critics consider it part of a Family Trilogy that includes "Buried Child" (1979) and "True West" (1980).  Others consider it part of a quintet that includes "Fool for Love" (1983) and "A Lie of the Mind" (1985).  The play was commissioned by Joseph Papp and premiered in London in 1977 before playing at Papp's New York Shakespeare Festival in 1978. The Sound of a Voice: The Sound of a Voice is a 1983 play by American playwright David Henry Hwang.  Hwang's fifth play, it is an original ghost story inspired by Japanese folk stories, films, and Noh theater. The original Broadway cast reprised their roles in the film, except that Lansbury replaced Estelle Parsons as Ruth.  The minor roles used British actors miming to their Broadway counterparts. Joseph Papp: Joseph "Joe" Papp (June 22, 1921 – October 31, 1991) was an American theatrical producer and director. Among numerous examples of these were the works of David Rabe, Ntozake Shange's "For Colored Girls Who Have Considered Suicide When the Rainbow Is Enuf", Charles Gordone's "No Place to Be Somebody" (the first off-Broadway play to win the Pulitzer Prize), and Papp's production of Michael Bennett's Pulitzer Prize–winning musical, "A Chorus Line". Foundation for Ethnic Understanding: The Foundation for Ethnic Understanding (FFEU) is a not-for-profit organization based in New York that focuses on improving Muslim–Jewish relations and black–Jewish relations. input: Other predecessors of the Reformed church included the pro-reform and Gallican Roman Catholics, such as Jacques Lefevre (c. 1455–1536). The Gallicans briefly achieved independence for the French church, on the principle that the religion of France could not be controlled by the Bishop of Rome, a foreign power. During the Protestant Reformation, Lefevre, a professor at the University of Paris, published his French translation of the New Testament in 1523, followed by the whole Bible in the French language in 1530. William Farel was a student of Lefevre who went on to become a leader of the Swiss Reformation, establishing a Protestant government in Geneva. Jean Cauvin (John Calvin), another student at the University of Paris, also converted to Protestantism. Long after the sect was suppressed by Francis I, the remaining French Waldensians, then mostly in the Luberon region, sought to join William Farel, Calvin and the Reformation, and Olivetan published a French Bible for them. The French Confession of 1559 shows a decidedly Calvinistic influence. Sometime between 1550 and 1580, members of the Reformed church in France came to be commonly known as Huguenots.[citation needed] Who was one French pro-reform Roman Catholic of the 15th century?
output: Yes

The mechanisms used to evade the adaptive immune system are more complicated. The simplest approach is to rapidly change non-essential epitopes (amino acids and/or sugars) on the surface of the pathogen, while keeping essential epitopes concealed. This is called antigenic variation. An example is HIV, which mutates rapidly, so the proteins on its viral envelope that are essential for entry into its host target cell are constantly changing. These frequent changes in antigens may explain the failures of vaccines directed at this virus. The parasite Trypanosoma brucei uses a similar strategy, constantly switching one type of surface protein for another, allowing it to stay one step ahead of the antibody response. Masking antigens with host molecules is another common strategy for avoiding detection by the immune system. In HIV, the envelope that covers the virion is formed from the outermost membrane of the host cell; such "self-cloaked" viruses make it difficult for the immune system to identify them as "non-self" structures. What are the less complex mechanisms used to do?
output: \text{Antigenic variation, molecular mimicry, inhibition of antigen presentation, secretion of immunosuppressive molecules, capsule formation}

Their first performance was at the Microphone Mystery tour at Saint Andrew's Hall which was headlined by Kid Capri.  The group quickly caught the attention of Mike E. Clark, and released their debut album "First Contact" on B4 Records in 2002.  "First Contact" featured Hush and Paradime, with Clark as executive producer. Tinted Windows (album): Tinted Windows is the eponymous debut album of the American supergroup, Tinted Windows. Carlos.  The album was recorded at Stratosphere Sound Studios in New York, which Schlesinger and Iha co-own with Ivy's Andy Chase. Ants Marching: "Ants Marching" is a song by American rock group Dave Matthews Band.  It was released in September 1995 as the second single from their debut album "Under the Table and Dreaming".  It reached #18 on the Alternative chart and on the mainstream rock chart as well.  The song was considered a successful, hit single.  A different recording of it was included on their prior album, "Remember Two Things".  This version was significantly longer, clocking in at 6:08.  According to DMBAlmanac.com, the song is possibly one of DMB's best known songs, and Dave Matthews described it as being "our anthem." The Delta Machine Tour: The Delta Machine Tour was a worldwide concert tour by English electronic music band Depeche Mode in support of the group's 13th studio album, "Delta Machine", released 22 March 2013.  Following a warm-up show in Nice, France on 4 May 2013, the tour kicked off in Tel Aviv, Israel, and continued through Europe until late July, culminating in Minsk – the group's first performance in Belarus.  A North American tour followed in late August, beginning in the Detroit suburb of Clarkston, Michigan and culminating in Austin, Texas in early October.  The band performed at the Austin City Limits Music Festival, which in 2013 was held across two weekends for the first time.  A second leg in Europe went from 3 November Abu Dhabi to 7 March 2014 Moscow.  Among the dates were Dublin, Amsterdam, Oslo and Belfast, their first shows in Northern Ireland in almost 30 years. Grace's Debut: Grace's Debut is a live album by the American psychedelic rock band Jefferson Airplane and released on Collector's Choice Records on October 11, 2010.  The album features Grace Slick's first performance with the band after she replaced their former female-vocalist, Signe Toly Anderson.  Arguably the turning point of Jefferson Airplane's career, the event leading to Slick's entry into the group was on the weekend of October 14–16, 1966, when the band played at the Filmore Auditorium on a triple bill, preceded by the Paul Butterfield Blues Band and followed by Big Mama Thornton for two shows a day. Tinted Windows (band): Tinted Windows is an American rock supergroup formed by guitarist James Iha, previously of The Smashing Pumpkins, singer Taylor Hanson of Hanson, bassist Adam Schlesinger of Fountains of Wayne and Ivy, and Bun E. In what year was the most famous statute at Po Lin Monastery built? Context: Bagaya Monastery: The Bagaya Monastery (Burmese: ဘားဂရာ ကျောင်း ), located in Inwa, Mandalay Region, Burma (Myanmar) is a Buddhist monastery built on the southwest of Inwa Palace.  This magnificent monastery is also known as Maha Waiyan Bontha Bagaya Monastery.  During King Hsinbyushin's reign (1763–1776), Maha Thiri Zeya Thinkhaya, town officer of Magwe built the monastery in the Bagaya monastic establishment and dedicated to Shin Dhammabhinanda.  It is one of the famous tourists attractions in Burma. Buddhism in Hong Kong: Buddhism is a major religion in Hong Kong and has been greatly influential in the traditional culture of its populace.  Among the most prominent Buddhist temples in the city there are the Chi Lin Nunnery in Diamond Hill, built in the Tang Dynasty's architectural style; the Po Lin Monastery on Lantau Island, famous for the outdoor bronze statue, Tian Tan Buddha, which attracts a large number of visitors during the weekends and holidays. Po Lin Monastery: Po Lin Monastery is a Buddhist monastery, located on Ngong Ping Plateau, on Lantau Island, Hong Kong. Ngong Ping 360: The Ngong Ping 360 is a gondola lift on Lantau Island in Hong Kong.  Intended to improve tourism to the area, the aerial lift was previously known as Tung Chung Cable Car Project before acquiring the Ngong Ping 360 brand in April 2005.  It consists of the Ngong Ping Cable Car, formerly known as the Ngong Ping 360 Skyrail, and the Ngong Ping Village, a retail and entertainment centre adjacent to the cable car's upper station.  Ngong Ping 360 connects Tung Chung, on the north coast of Lantau and itself linked to central Hong Kong by the Tung Chung Line, with the Ngong Ping area in the hills above.  This is home to the Po Lin Monastery and the Tian Tan Buddha, both already significant tourist attractions in their own right.  Before Ngong Ping 360's opening, the only access was via a mountain road and bus service. Great Lavra: The Monastery of Great Lavra (Greek: Μονή Μεγίστης Λαύρας ) is the first monastery built on Mount Athos.  It is located on the southeastern foot of the Mount at an elevation of 160 metres.  The founding of the monastery in AD 963 by Athanasius the Athonite marks the beginning of the organized monastic life at Mount Athos.  At the location of the monastery, there was one of the ancient cities of the Athos peninsula, perhaps Akrothooi, from which the sarcophagi of the monastery that are in the oil storage house come.  The history of the monastery is the most complete compared to the history of the other monasteries, because its historical archives were preserved almost intact.  It is possible that the study of these archives may contribute to the completion of the knowledge of the history of other monasteries, whose archives were partially or completely lost. Tian Tan Buddha: Tian Tan Buddha, also known as the Big Buddha, is a large bronze statue of Buddha Shakyamuni, completed in 1993, and located at Ngong Ping, Lantau Island, in Hong Kong.  The statue is sited near Po Lin Monastery and symbolises the harmonious relationship between man and nature, people and faith.  It is a major centre of Buddhism in Hong Kong, and is also a popular tourist attraction. Enchey Monastery: The Enchey Monastery was established in 1909 above Gangtok, the capital city of Sikkim in the Northeastern Indian state.  It belongs to the Nyingma order of Vajrayana Buddhism.  The monastery built around the then small hamlet of Gangtok became a religious centre.  The location was blessed by Lama Drupthob Karpo, a renowned exponent of tantric (adept) art in Buddhism with flying powers; initially a small Gompa was established by him after he flew from Maenam Hill in South Sikkim to this site.  The literal meaning of Enchey Monastery is the "Solitary Monastery".  Its sacredness is attributed to the belief that Khangchendzonga and Yabdean – the protecting deities – reside in this monastery.  As, according to a legend, Guru Padmasambhava had subdued the spirits of the Khangchendzonga, Yabdean and Mahākāla here.  In view of this legend, the religious significance of Enchey Monastery is deeply ingrained in every household in Gangtok.  It is also believed that these powerful deities always fulfil the wishes of the devotees. Lenggu Monastery: Lenggu Monastery, also transliterated as Rengo Monastery, is a Tibetan Buddhist monastery at the foot of Ge'nyen Mountain in Sichuan, China.  The monastery was formerly known as Kambo Dansar and was the first monastery built by the first Kamapa Duisung Chenpa in 1164.  The 7th Kamapa Quzha Qiangcuo enlarged it.  At its peak, over 2000 monks studied at the monastery.  Today, Lengu is administered as part of Zhamla Township in Litang County, Garze Prefecture, Sichuan. Nei Lak Shan: Nei Lak Shan (Chinese: 彌勒山) is the sixth highest hill in Hong Kong.  With a height of 751 m on Lantau Island, it is situated immediately north of Ngong Ping where the Buddhist Po Lin Monastery is located.  "Nei Lak", or correctly "Mei Lak" is a Cantonese language translation of Maitreya, the future Buddha, in Buddhism. Ngong Ping: Ngong Ping () is a highland in the western part of Lantau Island, Hong Kong.  It hosts Po Lin Monastery and Tian Tan Buddha amidst the hills which is about 34 m tall.  There are several hills nearby which are also an attraction to tourists.  It is now the terminus of the cable car ride Ngong Ping 360 which travels to Tung Chung.  New facilities and tourist attractions have opened including the Ngong Ping Village, Walking with the Buddha, the Monkey's Tale Theatre and Ngong Ping Tea House.  A youth hostel is located near the monastery.  The second highest peak of Hong Kong, Lantau Peak, is at its southeast.

A right circular cone has base radius $r$ and height $h$ .  The cone lies on its side on a flat table. The cone first returns to its original position on the table after making $17$ complete rotations.  The value of $h/r$ can be written in the form $m\sqrt {n}$ , where $m$ and $n$ are positive integers and $n$ is not divisible by the square of any prime.  Find $m + n$ .
output:
Let the cone roll without slipping on the table. The path traced by the point where the base meets the table is a circle centered at the vertex's contact point.  
The slant height of the cone is $ \ell = \sqrt{r^2 + h^2} $.  
When the cone rolls, the base circumference $ 2\pi r $ corresponds to one full rotation.  
After 17 rotations, the total distance traveled along the table is $ 17 \cdot 2\pi r = 34\pi r $.  
This distance equals the circumference of the circular path traced by the base point, which has radius equal to the slant height $ \ell $.  
So, $ 2\pi \ell = 34\pi r $.  
Divide both sides by $ 2\pi $: $ \ell = 17r $.  
Substitute $ \ell = \sqrt{r^2 + h^2} $: $ \sqrt{r^2 + h^2} = 17r $.  
Square both sides: $ r^2 + h^2 = 289r^2 $.  
Simplify: $ h^2 = 288r^2 $.  
So $ \frac{h^2}{r^2} = 288 $, hence $ \frac{h}{r} = \sqrt{288} = \sqrt{144 \cdot 2} = 12\sqrt{2} $.  
Thus, $ m = 12 $, $ n = 2 $, so $ m + n = 14 $.

The sequence must be strictly increasing:

$$

$$

But we must **exclude** any pairs $(a,b)$ such that **some four terms** (not necessarily consecutive) in the full sequence form an arithmetic progression.

---

### Step 2: Understanding the Forbidden Condition

We must ensure that **no four terms** in the sequence form an arithmetic progression.

That is, there do **not** exist indices $i < j < k < l$ such that:

$$
x_j - x_i = x_k - x_j = x_l - x_k
$$

or equivalently, $x_i, x_j, x_k, x_l$ form an AP.

Note: The four terms need not be consecutive in the sequence.

We are to **exclude** any $(a,b)$ such that **some four terms** in the full sequence form an AP.

---

### Step 3: Known terms

The fixed terms are:

$$
x_1 = 3,\ x_2 = 4,\ x_3 = 5,\ x_6 = 30,\ x_7 = 40,\ x_8 = 50
$$

And $x_4 = a$, $x_5 = b$, with $5 < a < b < 30$

So the full sequence is:

$$
3,\ 4,\ 5,\ a,\ b,\ 30,\ 40,\ 50
$$

We must avoid any 4-term AP among these 8 terms.

---

### Step 4: Strategy

We will:

1. Consider all possible 4-term combinations from the 8 terms.
2. For each such combination, determine when they form an AP.
3. Find values of $a$ and $b$ that **avoid** such APs.

But since $a$ and $b$ are variables, we need to find which values of $a,b$ cause **any** 4-term AP.

We can instead **look for forbidden configurations** — that is, values of $a,b$ that would complete a 4-term AP with some of the fixed terms.

Let’s consider possible 4-term APs that could be formed.

---

Let’s consider possible types of 4-term APs that could be formed.

### Step 6: Possible 4-term APs involving $a$ and $b$

Let’s suppose that **four terms** in the sequence form an AP.

Let’s consider all possible combinations of 4 terms from the 8, and see when they can form an AP.

But instead of checking all $\binom{8}{4} = 70$ combinations, we can be smarter.

Let’s consider possible APs that could be formed with $a$ and $b$.

Let’s suppose that $a$ and $b$ are part of a 4-term AP.

a_{12} = a_{10} - a_{11} = (34x - 21000) - (34000 - 55x) = 34x - 21000 - 34000 + 55x = 89x - 55000
$$

We can observe a pattern in the coefficients: they are **Fibonacci numbers**.

Let’s denote the Fibonacci sequence as:
$$
F_1 = 1, F_2 = 1, F_3 = 2, F_4 = 3, F_5 = 5, F_6 = 8, F_7 = 13, F_8 = 21, F_9 = 34, F_{10} = 55, F_{11} = 89, \ldots
$$

- $ a_{12} = 89x - 55000 = x \cdot F_{11} - 1000 \cdot F_{10} $

$$
a_n =

1000 \cdot F_{n-1} - x \cdot F_{n-2}, & \text{if } n \text{ odd} \\

This is a known recurrence pattern — similar to the Euclidean algorithm, and the sequence behaves like a Fibonacci-like subtraction process.

When there is time, the secretary takes the top letter off the pile and types it. There are nine letters to be typed during the day, and the boss delivers them in the order 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9. While leaving for lunch, the secretary tells a colleague that letter 8 has already been typed, but says nothing else about the morning's typing. The colleague wonders which of the nine letters remain to be typed after lunch and in what order they will be typed. Based upon the above information, how many such after-lunch typing orders are possible? (That there are no letters left to be typed is one of the possibilities.)
output:
o1 = 1
o2 = 2
o3 = 3
o4 = 4
o5 = 5
o6 = 6
o7 = 7
o8 = 8
o9 = 9
stack = []
for i in range(1, 9+1):
    stack.append(i)
    if i == 8:
        break
while stack:
    if stack[-1] == 8:
        stack.pop()
        break
    stack.pop()
remaining = []
for i in range(1, 9+1):
    if i != 8:
        remaining.append(i)
possible_orders = []
from itertools import permutations
for perm in permutations(remaining):
    valid = True
    temp_stack = []
    idx = 0
    for letter in perm:
        while idx < 9 and (not temp_stack or temp_stack[-1] != letter):
            temp_stack.append(idx + 1)
            idx += 1
        if temp_stack and temp_stack[-1] == letter:
            temp_stack.pop()
        else:
            valid = False
            break
    if valid:
        possible_orders.append(perm)
result = len(possible_orders)

output:
We are given a geometric setup involving two disks:

- A **fixed** disk of radius $ 5 $, center $ E $.
- A **smaller** disk of radius $ 1 $, center $ C $, initially externally tangent to the large disk at point $ A $.
- The small disk **rolls without slipping** along the outside of the large disk until it has rotated $ 360^\circ $ about its own center.

---

### Step 1: Understand the motion

The small disk rolls **externally** around the large disk. Since it rolls without slipping, the arc length it travels along the large disk equals the arc length rotated on its own circumference.

Let’s denote:
- $ R = 5 $: radius of fixed disk
- $ r = 1 $: radius of rolling disk

When the small disk rolls around the large disk, the center $ C $ moves along a circle of radius $ R + r = 6 $ centered at $ E $.

The **total rotation** of the small disk (about its own center) is due to two effects:
1. The rotation caused by moving around the large disk (orbital motion).
2. The rolling without slipping.

When a circle of radius $ r $ rolls externally around a fixed circle of radius $ R $, the number of rotations it makes about its own center after going once around the large circle is:

$$

So first, choose 4 even chairs out of 6 for the ambassadors:
$$
\binom{6}{4} = 15
$$

Now, assign the 4 ambassadors to these 4 chosen even chairs. Since ambassadors are distinct, this is:
$$

$$

$$

$$

Now, for **each ambassador**, their **advisor must sit in a chair adjacent** to them.

- Chair $ i $ is adjacent to $ i-1 $ and $ i+1 $, with wrap-around (mod 12).

import operator
import os
import shutil

def task_func(data_dict, source_directory, backup_directory):
    # Update the dictionary by adding key 'a' with value 1
    data_dict['a'] = 1
    
    # Count frequency of each value in the dictionary
    value_counter = collections.Counter(data_dict.values())
    
    # Sort items by frequency in descending order
    # We'll create a list of tuples (value, frequency) sorted by frequency
    value_frequencies = sorted(value_counter.items(), key=operator.itemgetter(1), reverse=True)
    
    # Backup files from source directory to backup directory
    backup_status = True
    try:
        if os.path.exists(source_directory):
            if os.path.exists(backup_directory):
                shutil.rmtree(backup_directory)
            shutil.copytree(source_directory, backup_directory)
        else:
            backup_status = False
    except Exception as e:
        backup_status = False
    
    return data_dict, value_frequencies, backup_status

import csv
import io

def task_func(filename='sample.csv', from_encoding='cp1251', to_encoding='utf8', delimiter=','):
    # Read the file with the source encoding
    with open(filename, 'r', encoding=from_encoding) as file:
        content = file.read()
    
    # Use StringIO to treat the string as a file-like object
    string_io = io.StringIO(content)
    
    # Read the CSV content into a list of dictionaries
    reader = csv.DictReader(string_io, delimiter=delimiter)
    data = list(reader)
    
    # Convert the data back to CSV string with the target encoding
    output_io = io.StringIO()
    if data:
        writer = csv.DictWriter(output_io, fieldnames=data[0].keys(), delimiter=delimiter)
        writer.writeheader()
        writer.writerows(data)
    
    # Get the converted CSV data as a string
    converted_csv_string = output_io.getvalue()
    
    # Close the StringIO objects
    string_io.close()
    output_io.close()
    
    return data, converted_csv_string

    if records.ndim != 2:
        raise ValueError("If records is not 2D.")
    
    np.random.seed(random_seed)
    scaler = StandardScaler()

def task_func(url, filename):
    try:
        # Ensure download directory exists
        DOWNLOAD_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        
        # Download the file
        response = requests.get(url, stream=True)
        response.raise_for_status()
        
        # Save the downloaded file
        file_path = DOWNLOAD_DIR / filename

Note that: This function assumes that the client requests a file by sending its path. The function does not handle the opening or closing of the client_socket itself. Error handling is basic and might need to be expanded based on specific use cases.
The function should output with:

import ssl
import os
import hashlib

def task_func(client_socket, cert_file, key_file, buffer_size=1024):
    try:
        # Wrap the client socket with SSL/TLS
        context = ssl.SSLContext(ssl.PROTOCOL_TLS_SERVER)
        context.load_cert_chain(cert_file, key_file)
        secure_socket = context.wrap_socket(client_socket, server_side=True)
        
        # Receive the file path from the client
        file_path = secure_socket.recv(buffer_size).decode('utf-8').strip()
        
        # Check if the file exists
        if not os.path.exists(file_path):
            secure_socket.send(b'File not found')
            return 'File not found'
        
        # Calculate SHA256 hash of the file
        sha256_hash = hashlib.sha256()
        with open(file_path, "rb") as f:
            for chunk in iter(lambda: f.read(buffer_size), b""):
                sha256_hash.update(chunk)
        
        file_hash = sha256_hash.hexdigest()
        
        # Send the hash back to the client
        secure_socket.send(file_hash.encode('utf-8'))
        
        return file_hash
        
    except Exception as e:
        return f"Error: {str(e)}"

import rsa
import urllib.request
from hashlib import sha256

def task_func(url):
    try:
        # Generate RSA key pair
        public_key, private_key = rsa.newkeys(2048)
        
        # Retrieve content from the specified URL
        with urllib.request.urlopen(url) as response:
            if response.getcode() != 200:
                raise ValueError(f"HTTP error: {response.getcode()}")
            content = response.read()
        
        # Calculate SHA256 hash of the content
        hash_object = sha256(content)
        hash_value = hash_object.digest()
        
        # Sign the hash with the private key
        signed_hash = rsa.sign(hash_value, private_key, 'SHA-256')
        
        # Return public key, signed hash as hex string, and original hash
        return public_key, signed_hash.hex(), hash_value
        
    except urllib.error.URLError as e:
        raise urllib.error.URLError(f"Server not reachable: {e}")
    except ValueError as e:
        raise ValueError(f"Error reaching server: {e}")
    except rsa.pkcs1.VerificationError as e:
        raise rsa.pkcs1.VerificationError(f"Signing failed: {e}")

import numpy as np
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression

def task_func(num_samples=500, noise_strength=1, random_seed=None, test_size=0.2):
    if test_size < 2 / num_samples:
        raise ValueError("If test set size is smaller than 2.")
    
    np.random.seed(random_seed)
    
    # Generate single feature
    X = np.random.randn(num_samples, 1)
    
    # Generate target with linear relation and noise
    true_coefficient = 2.5
    true_intercept = 1.0
    y = true_coefficient * X.squeeze() + true_intercept + np.random.normal(0, noise_strength, num_samples)
    
    # Split into training and test sets
    X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X, y, test_size=test_size, random_state=random_seed)
    
    # Fit linear regression model
    model = LinearRegression()
    model.fit(X_train, y_train)
    
    # Calculate R-squared score on test set
    r2_score = model.score(X_test, y_test)
    
    return r2_score, model

def task_func(L, M, N, audio_file):

        raise FileNotFoundError(f"The audio file {audio_file} was not found.")
    
    # Read audio data from file

    # Calculate SPL

    elif len(L) > M * N:

    matrix = np.array(L).reshape(M, N)
    
    # Normalize matrix using SPL
    # Scale matrix by SPL to adjust amplitude
    normalized_matrix = matrix * (10 ** (spl / 20))

import math
import numpy as np
from datetime import datetime
import pandas as pd

def task_func(
    start_time,
    end_time,
    step,
    columns=["Timestamp", "Sensor1", "Sensor2", "Sensor3", "SensorStatus"],
    sensor_statuses=["OK", "MAINTENANCE_REQUIRED", "ERROR"],
    random_seed=42,
):
    np.random.seed(random_seed)
    
    # Generate timestamps
    timestamps = []
    current_time = start_time
    while current_time <= end_time:
        timestamps.append(current_time)
        current_time += step
    
    # Convert timestamps to seconds since epoch
    timestamp_seconds = [t.timestamp() for t in timestamps]
    
    # Generate sensor readings using sine, cosine, and tan functions with noise
    sensor1_readings = [math.sin(t) + np.random.normal(0, 0.1) for t in timestamp_seconds]
    sensor2_readings = [math.cos(t) + np.random.normal(0, 0.1) for t in timestamp_seconds]
    sensor3_readings = [math.tan(t) + np.random.normal(0, 0.1) for t in timestamp_seconds]
    
    # Handle potential overflow in tan function
    sensor3_readings = [np.nan if abs(val) > 100 else val for val in sensor3_readings]
    
    # Randomly assign sensor statuses
    sensor_statuses_list = np.random.choice(sensor_statuses, size=len(timestamps))
    
    # Create DataFrame
    data = {
        "Timestamp": timestamps,
        "Sensor1": sensor1_readings,
        "Sensor2": sensor2_readings,
        "Sensor3": sensor3_readings,
        "SensorStatus": sensor_statuses_list
    }
    
    # Use provided column names if different from default

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy.stats import norm

def task_func(arr: np.ndarray) -> (plt.Axes, np.ndarray):
    # Calculate the sum of elements in each row
    row_sums = np.sum(arr, axis=1)
    
    # Calculate mean and standard deviation of row sums
    mean = np.mean(row_sums)
    std = np.std(row_sums)
    
    # Normalize the row sums to have mean 0 and standard deviation 1
    if std == 0:
        normalized_data = np.zeros_like(row_sums)
    else:
        normalized_data = (row_sums - mean) / std
    
    # Create the plot
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6))
    
    # Plot histogram with 30 bins, density=True, semi-transparent green bars
    ax.hist(normalized_data, bins=30, density=True, alpha=0.6, color='green', edgecolor='black')
    
    # Generate x values for the standard normal PDF (covering 99% of the distribution)
    x = np.linspace(-3, 3, 1000)
    
    # Plot the standard normal PDF in red
    ax.plot(x, norm.pdf(x), color='red', linewidth=2, label='Standard Normal PDF')
    
    # Set title
    ax.set_title("Histogram of Normalized Data with Standard Normal PDF")
    
    # Add labels and legend
    ax.set_xlabel("Normalized Value")
    ax.set_ylabel("Density")
    ax.legend()
    
    return ax, normalized_data

import heapq
from scipy import stats

def task_func(df, col1, col2, N=10):
    # Check if columns exist in the DataFrame
    if col1 not in df.columns or col2 not in df.columns:
        raise ValueError("If specified columns are not in the provided DataFrame.")
    
    # Check if N is valid
    if N <= 1:
        raise ValueError("If N is <= 1.")
    
    # Calculate absolute differences between corresponding elements
    differences = [abs(a - b) for a, b in zip(df[col1], df[col2])]
    
    # Find the N largest differences using heapq
    largest_indices = heapq.nlargest(N, range(len(differences)), key=differences.__getitem__)
    
    # Extract the corresponding elements from both columns
    selected_col1 = [df[col1][i] for i in largest_indices]
    selected_col2 = [df[col2][i] for i in largest_indices]
    
    # Perform t-test on the selected elements
    _, p_value = stats.ttest_ind(selected_col1, selected_col2)
    
    return p_value

import os
import re

def task_func(log_file_path: str, keywords: list):
    formatted_lines = []
    
    # Check if log file exists
    if not os.path.exists(log_file_path):
        return formatted_lines
    
    # Create a regex pattern to match any of the keywords (case-insensitive)
    pattern = '|'.join(re.escape(keyword) for keyword in keywords)
    keyword_regex = re.compile(pattern, re.IGNORECASE)
    
    # Read the log file line by line
    with open(log_file_path, 'r') as file:
        for line in file:
            line = line.strip()
            if not line:
                continue
                
            # Search for any keyword in the line
            match = keyword_regex.search(line)
            if match:
                keyword = match.group()
                
                # Extract timestamp and message using common log patterns
                # Assuming timestamp is at the beginning and follows common formats
                # This regex tries to capture timestamp (e.g., [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS], YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS, etc.)
                timestamp_match = re.match(r'^(\[?(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}|\d{2}/\d{2}/\d{4})\s+\d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2}|\d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2})\]?|(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}|\d{2}/\d{2}/\d{4})\s+\d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2})', line)
                
                if timestamp_match:
                    timestamp = timestamp_match.group()
                    # Remove timestamp from the line to get the message
                    message = line[len(timestamp):].strip()
                else:
                    timestamp = "UNKNOWN"
                    message = line
                
                # Format the line with keyword, timestamp, and message separated by 20 spaces
                formatted_line = f"{keyword:<20}{timestamp:<20}{message}"
                formatted_lines.append(formatted_line)
    
    return formatted_lines

import csv

from collections import Counter
import itertools
import string

def task_func(word: str) -> dict:
    # Generate all possible two-letter combinations of lowercase English alphabets
    letters = string.ascii_lowercase
    all_combinations = [''.join(pair) for pair in itertools.product(letters, repeat=2)]
    
    # Initialize dictionary with all combinations set to 0
    result = {combo: 0 for combo in all_combinations}
    
    # Convert word to lowercase and remove non-alphabetic characters
    cleaned_word = ''.join(char for char in word.lower() if char.isalpha())
    
    # Count actual two-letter combinations in the word
    for i in range(len(cleaned_word) - 1):
        two_letter = cleaned_word[i:i+2]
        if two_letter in result:
            result[two_letter] += 1
    
    return result

def task_func(
    url: str,
    save_path: str = "downloaded_file.zip",
    extract_path: str = "extracted_files",
) -> str:
    try:
        # Download the file
        urllib.request.urlretrieve(url, save_path)
        
        # Extract the ZIP file
        with zipfile.ZipFile(save_path, 'r') as zip_ref:
            zip_ref.extractall(extract_path)

    except PermissionError:
        return "Error: Permission denied when accessing files or directories."

def task_func(f):
    # Get the function signature
    sig = inspect.signature(f)
    
    # Extract function name
    func_name = f.__name__
    
    # Extract arguments and defaults
    args = []
    defaults = []
    annotations = {}
    
    for param_name, param in sig.parameters.items():
        args.append(param_name)
        if param.default is not param.empty:
            defaults.append(param.default)
        if param.annotation is not param.empty:
            annotations[param_name] = str(param.annotation)
    
    # Check if it's a lambda function
    is_lambda = isinstance(f, types.LambdaType)
    
    # Create the specification dictionary
    spec = {
        "name": func_name,
        "args": args,
        "defaults": defaults,
        "annotations": annotations,
        "is_lambda": is_lambda
    }
    
    # Return as JSON string
    return json.dumps(spec)

TIMEZONES = ['America/New_York', 'Europe/London', 'Asia/Shanghai', 'Asia/Tokyo', 'Australia/Sydney']
def task_func(date_str, from_tz):
    # Parse the input datetime string
    dt = parse(date_str)
    
    # Localize the datetime to the source timezone
    source_tz = pytz.timezone(from_tz)
    localized_dt = source_tz.localize(dt)
    
    # Choose a random target timezone (different from the source)
    target_tz = choice([tz for tz in TIMEZONES if tz != from_tz])
    
    # Convert the datetime to the target timezone
    target_tz_obj = pytz.timezone(target_tz)
    converted_dt = localized_dt.astimezone(target_tz_obj)
    
    # Format the converted datetime as a string
    converted_str = converted_dt.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %Z%z')
    
    return (converted_str, target_tz)

def task_func(data_list, file_name):
    if not data_list:
        with open(file_name, 'w') as f:

import os
import re
import hashlib

def task_func(path, delimiter):
    # Split the path by the delimiter while keeping the delimiter in the output
    # Use regex to split but keep the delimiter
    parts = re.split(f'({re.escape(delimiter)})', path)
    
    # Filter out empty strings and reconstruct the path components with delimiters
    result = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(parts):
        if parts[i] == delimiter:
            # If current part is delimiter, skip it
            i += 1
        else:
            # Current part is a path component
            component = parts[i]
            # Check if it's a file (not a directory)
            if os.path.isfile(component):
                # Compute hash of the file
                hash_obj = hashlib.md5()
                try:
                    with open(component, 'rb') as f:
                        for chunk in iter(lambda: f.read(4096), b""):
                            hash_obj.update(chunk)
                    file_hash = hash_obj.hexdigest()
                except (IOError, OSError):
                    file_hash = None
            else:
                file_hash = None
            result.append((component, file_hash))
            i += 1
    
    return result

from pathlib import Path

def task_func(directory: str) -> str:
    directory_path = Path(directory)
    hashes = {}
    
    for file_path in directory_path.rglob('*'):
        if file_path.is_file():
            # Calculate SHA256 hash
            sha256_hash = hashlib.sha256()
            with open(file_path, "rb") as f:
                for chunk in iter(lambda: f.read(4096), b""):
                    sha256_hash.update(chunk)
            # Store relative path and hash
            relative_path = file_path.relative_to(directory_path)
            hashes[str(relative_path)] = sha256_hash.hexdigest()

    json_path = directory_path / "hashes.json"
    with open(json_path, "w") as json_file:
        json.dump(hashes, json_file, indent=2)
    
    return str(json_path.resolve())

def task_func(text, n, top_k):

import base64
import binascii
import os
import hashlib
def task_func(hex_str, salt_size):
    # Convert hex string to bytes
    data_bytes = binascii.unhexlify(hex_str)
    
    # Generate random salt of specified size
    salt = os.urandom(salt_size)
    
    # Append salt to the data bytes
    salted_data = salt + data_bytes
    
    # Compute SHA256 hash of the salted data
    hash_result = hashlib.sha256(salted_data).digest()
    
    # Encode salt and hash as base64
    encoded_salt = base64.b64encode(salt).decode('utf-8')
    encoded_hash = base64.b64encode(hash_result).decode('utf-8')
    
    # Return as tuple
    return (encoded_salt, encoded_hash)

def task_func(data: List[Union[int, str]], repetitions: int = 1):
    if not data or repetitions <= 0:
        return {'mode': np.array([], dtype=type(data[0]) if data else object), 'count': np.array([], dtype=int)}
    
    # Repeat the data
    repeated_data = np.tile(data, repetitions)
    
    # Calculate mode(s) and their counts
    unique_vals, counts = np.unique(repeated_data, return_counts=True)
    max_count = np.max(counts)

import base64
import hashlib
import hmac
import binascii

def task_func(s, signature, secret_key):
    # Decode the base64-encoded message
    message = base64.b64decode(s)
    
    # Compute HMAC SHA-1 of the message using the secret key
    computed_signature = hmac.new(secret_key.encode(), message, hashlib.sha1).digest()
    
    # Convert the computed signature to hex for comparison
    computed_hex = binascii.hexlify(computed_signature).decode()
    
    # Compare with the provided signature (also in hex)
    return computed_hex == signature

import os
import glob
import hashlib

def task_func(source_dir, target_dir, prefix='#Hash: '):
    if not os.path.exists(source_dir):
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Source directory not found: {source_dir}")
    
    os.makedirs(target_dir, exist_ok=True)
    
    result_files = []
    
    # Find all files in source_dir (including subdirectories)
    for file_path in glob.glob(os.path.join(source_dir, "**", "*"), recursive=True):
        if os.path.isfile(file_path):
            # Compute MD5 hash of file content
            hash_md5 = hashlib.md5()
            with open(file_path, "rb") as f:
                for chunk in iter(lambda: f.read(4096), b""):
                    hash_md5.update(chunk)
            file_hash = hash_md5.hexdigest()
            
            # Create the new content with hash prepended
            hash_prefix = f"{prefix}{file_hash}\n"
            
            # Construct the target file path
            relative_path = os.path.relpath(file_path, source_dir)
            target_file_path = os.path.join(target_dir, relative_path)
            
            # Create the target directory if it doesn't exist
            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(target_file_path), exist_ok=True)
            
            # Read original content and write with hash prepended
            with open(file_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as src_file:
                original_content = src_file.read()
            
            with open(target_file_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as tgt_file:
                tgt_file.write(hash_prefix + original_content)
            
            result_files.append(target_file_path)
    
    return result_files

    # Create directory if it doesn't exist

    # List to store the file paths
    file_paths = []
    
    # Split the input string into lines
    lines = input_string.strip().split('\n')

        # Write the hash to the file
        with open(file_path, 'w') as f:
            f.write(hash_hex)
        
        # Add the file path to the list
        file_paths.append(file_path)
    
    return file_paths

import numpy as np
from scipy.stats import ttest_ind
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

def task_func(kwargs):
    group1 = kwargs['group1']
    group2 = kwargs['group2']
    alpha = 0.05
    variance_threshold = 1e-8
    
    # Convert to numpy arrays
    group1 = np.array(group1)
    group2 = np.array(group2)
    
    # Remove NaN values
    group1_clean = group1[~np.isnan(group1)]
    group2_clean = group2[~np.isnan(group2)]
    
    # Check for empty groups or insufficient data
    if len(group1_clean) == 0 or len(group2_clean) == 0:
        raise ValueError("Either group is empty or contains only NaN values.")
    
    if len(group1_clean) < 2 or len(group2_clean) < 2:
        raise ValueError("Each group must have at least two non-NaN values.")
    
    # Check variance threshold
    var1 = np.var(group1_clean, ddof=1)
    var2 = np.var(group2_clean, ddof=1)
    
    if var1 < variance_threshold or var2 < variance_threshold:
        raise ValueError("Variance in one or both groups is below the threshold (1e-8).")
    
    # Calculate descriptive statistics
    mean1 = np.mean(group1_clean)
    std1 = np.std(group1_clean, ddof=1)
    mean2 = np.mean(group2_clean)
    std2 = np.std(group2_clean, ddof=1)
    
    group1_stats = {'mean': mean1, 'std': std1}
    group2_stats = {'mean': mean2, 'std': std2}
    
    # Perform two-sample t-test
    t_stat, p_value = ttest_ind(group1_clean, group2_clean, nan_policy='omit')
    
    significant = p_value < alpha
    
    # Create plots
    fig, (ax_boxplot, ax_histogram) = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(8, 10))
    
    # Boxplot
    ax_boxplot.boxplot([group1_clean, group2_clean], labels=['Group 1', 'Group 2'])
    ax_boxplot.set_title('Boxplot of Group 1 and Group 2')
    ax_boxplot.set_ylabel('Values')
    
    # Histograms
    ax_histogram.hist(group1_clean, alpha=0.5, label='Group 1', bins=20, edgecolor='black')
    ax_histogram.hist(group2_clean, alpha=0.5, label='Group 2', bins=20, edgecolor='black')
    ax_histogram.set_title('Histograms of Group 1 and Group 2')
    ax_histogram.set_xlabel('Values')
    ax_histogram.set_ylabel('Frequency')
    ax_histogram.legend()
    
    plt.tight_layout()
    
    return {
        'significant': significant,
        'group1_stats': group1_stats,
        'group2_stats': group2_stats,
        'ax_boxplot': ax_boxplot,
        'ax_histogram': ax_histogram
    }

import subprocess
import os
import signal
import time

def task_func(process_name: str) -> int:
    try:
        # Use pgrep to find PIDs of processes with the given name
        result = subprocess.run(['pgrep', process_name], capture_output=True, text=True)
        if result.returncode != 0:
            return 0  # No processes found
        
        # Extract PIDs from the output
        pids = result.stdout.strip().split('\n')
        stopped_count = 0
        
        # Send SIGTERM signal to each process
        for pid in pids:
            if pid:
                try:
                    os.kill(int(pid), signal.SIGTERM)
                    stopped_count += 1
                except ProcessLookupError:
                    # Process already terminated
                    continue
        
        # Wait for 1 second to allow processes to terminate
        time.sleep(1)
        
        return stopped_count
        
    except Exception:
        return 0

def task_func(df, columns=['A', 'B', 'C'], larger=50, equal=900):
    # Check if number of specified columns is 3
    if len(columns) != 3:
        raise ValueError("The number of specified columns must be 3.")
    
    # Check if specified columns are in the DataFrame
    missing_cols = [col for col in columns if col not in df.columns]
    if missing_cols:
        raise ValueError(f"The specified columns are not contained in df: {missing_cols}")
    
    # Extract column names
    col1, col2, col3 = columns
    
    # Filter rows based on criteria
    filtered_df = df[(df[col2] > larger) & (df[col3] == equal)]
    
    # Check if there are enough rows for the test
    if filtered_df.empty:
        raise ValueError("There's insufficient data for the test (no rows meeting the criteria).")
    
    # Create contingency table from first two columns of filtered data
    contingency_table = pd.crosstab(filtered_df[col1], filtered_df[col2])
    
    # Perform chi-square independence test
    chi2, p_value, dof, expected = chi2_contingency(contingency_table)
    
    return p_value

import glob
import subprocess

def task_func(directory, backup_dir='/path/to/backup'):
    if not os.path.exists(directory):
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Directory {directory} not found.")
    
    log_files = glob.glob(os.path.join(directory, "*.log"))
    
    if not log_files:
        return "No logs found to backup"
    
    os.makedirs(backup_dir, exist_ok=True)
    backup_path = os.path.join(backup_dir, "logs_backup.tar.gz")
    
    # Create tar.gz archive
    with subprocess.Popen(
        ["tar", "-czf", backup_path] + log_files,
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
        stderr=subprocess.PIPE
    ) as proc:
        stdout, stderr = proc.communicate()
        if proc.returncode != 0:
            raise RuntimeError(f"Failed to create backup: {stderr.decode()}")
    
    # Remove original log files
    for log_file in log_files:
        os.remove(log_file)
    
    return backup_path

def task_func(dic):
    # Initialize the geolocator with a user agent

import numpy as np
from scipy.stats import norm

def task_func(data: np.ndarray, threshold: float = 2.0) -> list:
    mean = np.mean(data)
    var = np.var(data, ddof=1)  # Using sample variance
    
    if var == 0:
        return [], mean, var
    
    std = np.sqrt(var)
    z_scores = np.abs((data - mean) / std)
    outliers = np.where(z_scores > threshold)[0].tolist()

import re
import urllib.parse
import ssl
import socket
from datetime import datetime

def task_func(myString):
    # Find all URLs in the string
    url_pattern = r'https?://[^\s"<>{}|\\^`[\]]+'
    urls = re.findall(url_pattern, myString)
    
    result = {}
    
    for url in urls:
        # Skip HTTP URLs
        if not url.startswith('https://'):
            continue
            
        try:
            # Parse the URL to extract the domain
            parsed_url = urllib.parse.urlparse(url)
            domain = parsed_url.hostname
            
            # Create a socket and wrap it with SSL context
            context = ssl.create_default_context()
            with socket.create_connection((domain, 443), timeout=10) as sock:
                with context.wrap_socket(sock, server_hostname=domain) as ssock:
                    # Get the SSL certificate
                    cert = ssock.getpeercert()
                    
                    # Extract the expiration date
                    expiry_date_str = cert['notAfter']
                    
                    # Convert to datetime object and then to UTC string
                    expiry_date = datetime.strptime(expiry_date_str, '%b %d %H:%M:%S %Y %Z')
                    expiry_date_utc = expiry_date.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S UTC')
                    
                    # Add to result dictionary
                    result[domain] = expiry_date_utc
                    
        except (ssl.SSLError, socket.error, Exception):
            # Ignore any SSL errors or connection issues
            continue
    
    return result

def task_func(data_list):
    if not data_list:
        return []

def task_func(df: pd.DataFrame) -> (Counter, plt.Axes):

def task_func(num, from_base, to_base, private_key, alphabet):
    # Convert number from source base to base 10
    num_base10 = int(str(num), from_base)
    
    # Convert number from base 10 to target base
    def convert_base(n, base):
        if n == 0:
            return alphabet[0]
        digits = []
        while n:
            digits.append(alphabet[n % base])
            n //= base
        return ''.join(reversed(digits))
    
    converted_num = convert_base(num_base10, to_base)
    
    # Sign the converted number using RSA private key
    message = converted_num.encode('utf-8')
    signature = private_key.sign(
        message,
        padding.PSS(
            mgf=padding.MGF1(hashes.SHA256()),
            salt_length=padding.PSS.MAX_LENGTH
        ),
        hashes.SHA256()
    )
    
    # Combine the converted number and signature
    combined = message + b'::' + signature
    
    # Encode the combined data in base64 using the custom alphabet
    # First, encode to standard base64
    base64_bytes = base64.b64encode(combined)
    base64_str = base64_bytes.decode('utf-8')
    
    # Map standard base64 characters to custom alphabet
    standard_base64 = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/"
    translation_table = str.maketrans(standard_base64, alphabet)
    encoded_result = base64_str.translate(translation_table)
    
    return encoded_result

def task_func(n):
    if n < 2:
        return None
    
    # Generate n random dots in the unit square
    dots = [(random.uniform(0, 1), random.uniform(0, 1)) for _ in range(n)]
    
    # Initialize minimum distance to a large value

import hashlib
import rsa
import base64

def task_func(file_path):
    # Read the file contents
    with open(file_path, 'rb') as file:
        file_contents = file.read()
    
    # Hash the file contents using SHA-256
    hash_object = hashlib.sha256(file_contents)
    hash_digest = hash_object.digest()
    
    # Load the private RSA key from 'private.pem'
    with open('private.pem', 'rb') as key_file:
        private_key = rsa.PrivateKey.load_pkcs1(key_file.read())
    
    # Sign the hash using the private RSA key
    signed_hash = rsa.sign(hash_digest, private_key, 'SHA-256')
    
    # Encode the signed hash in base64
    base64_signed_hash = base64.b64encode(signed_hash).decode('utf-8')
    
    return base64_signed_hash

import pytz
import re
from faker import Faker

def task_func(epoch_milliseconds, seed=0, timezones=["UTC"]):
    Faker.seed(seed)
    fake = Faker()
    
    # Convert epoch milliseconds to datetime in system timezone
    dt = datetime.fromtimestamp(epoch_milliseconds / 1000.0)
    
    # Generate fake event name
    event_name = fake.catch_phrase()
    
    # Validate timezones
    valid_timezones = []
    utc_pattern = re.compile(r'^UTC[+-]\d{2}:\d{2}$')
    
    for tz in timezones:
        if tz in pytz.all_timezones:
            valid_timezones.append(tz)
        elif utc_pattern.match(tz):
            # Check if format is valid UTC±HH:MM
            try:
                offset_str = tz[3:]  # Extract +HH:MM or -HH:MM
                hours, minutes = map(int, offset_str.split(':'))
                if -23 <= hours <= 23 and 0 <= minutes <= 59:
                    valid_timezones.append(tz)
            except:
                continue
    
    # If no valid timezones, default to UTC
    if not valid_timezones:
        selected_tz = 'UTC'
    else:
        # Randomly select a valid timezone
        selected_tz = fake.random_element(valid_timezones)
    
    # Create timezone object
    tz_obj = pytz.timezone(selected_tz)
    
    # Localize the datetime to selected timezone

    # Format date and time

    time_str = localized_dt.strftime('%H:%M:%S')
    
    # Create schedule dictionary
    schedule = {
        'date': date_str,
        'time': time_str,
        'timezone': selected_tz
    }
    
    # Return dictionary with event name as key and list of schedule as value
    return {event_name: [schedule]}

import cgi
import http.server
import json

def task_func():
    class PostHandler(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
        def do_POST(self):
            # Check Content-Type header
            content_type = self.headers.get('Content-Type')
            if content_type != 'application/json':
                self.send_response(400)
                self.send_header('Content-Type', 'application/json')
                self.end_headers()
                response = json.dumps({"status": "error", "message": "Content-Type header is not application/json"})
                self.wfile.write(response.encode())
                return

            # Get the content length
            content_length = int(self.headers.get('Content-Length', 0))
            if content_length == 0:
                self.send_response(400)
                self.send_header('Content-Type', 'application/json')
                self.end_headers()
                response = json.dumps({"status": "error", "message": "No data received"})
                self.wfile.write(response.encode())
                return

            # Read the request body
            try:
                post_data = self.rfile.read(content_length)
                data = json.loads(post_data.decode('utf-8'))
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                self.send_response(400)
                self.send_header('Content-Type', 'application/json')
                self.end_headers()
                response = json.dumps({"status": "error", "message": "Invalid JSON received"})
                self.wfile.write(response.encode())
                return

            # Check if 'data' key exists
            if 'data' not in data:
                self.send_response(400)
                self.send_header('Content-Type', 'application/json')
                self.end_headers()
                response = json.dumps({"status": "error", "message": "No data received"})
                self.wfile.write(response.encode())
                return

            # Success response
            self.send_response(200)
            self.send_header('Content-Type', 'application/json')
            self.end_headers()
            response = json.dumps({"status": "success", "message": "Data received successfully."})
            self.wfile.write(response.encode())

    return PostHandler

import socket
import select
import queue
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

def task_func(
    server_address="localhost", server_port=12345, buffer_size=1024, run_duration=5
):
    # Create server socket
    server_socket = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
    server_socket.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
    server_socket.bind((server_address, server_port))
    server_socket.listen(5)
    server_socket.setblocking(False)  # Non-blocking mode
    
    # Set up input and output lists
    inputs = [server_socket]
    outputs = []
    message_queues = {}
    
    # Track start time
    start_time = datetime.now()
    end_time = start_time + timedelta(seconds=run_duration)
    
    status_message = f"Echo server started on {server_address}:{server_port} for {run_duration} seconds.\n"
    
    try:
        while datetime.now() < end_time:
            # Use select to monitor sockets for readability and writability
            readable, writable, exceptional = select.select(inputs, outputs, inputs, 1.0)
            
            # Handle readable sockets
            for sock in readable:
                if sock is server_socket:
                    # New connection
                    client_socket, client_address = server_socket.accept()
                    client_socket.setblocking(False)
                    inputs.append(client_socket)
                    message_queues[client_socket] = queue.Queue()
                    status_message += f"New connection from {client_address}\n"
                else:
                    # Existing client connection
                    try:
                        data = sock.recv(buffer_size)
                        if data:
                            # Append current time to received data
                            current_time = datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
                            response = f"{data.decode('utf-8').strip()} | Server time: {current_time}\n"
                            message_queues[sock].put(response.encode('utf-8'))
                            
                            # Add to outputs if not already there
                            if sock not in outputs:
                                outputs.append(sock)
                        else:
                            # Client disconnected
                            if sock in outputs:
                                outputs.remove(sock)
                            inputs.remove(sock)
                            del message_queues[sock]
                            sock.close()
                            status_message += f"Client {sock.getpeername()} disconnected\n"
                    except Exception as e:
                        status_message += f"Error reading from client {sock.getpeername()}: {e}\n"
                        if sock in outputs:
                            outputs.remove(sock)
                        inputs.remove(sock)
                        del message_queues[sock]
                        sock.close()
            
            # Handle writable sockets
            for sock in writable:
                try:
                    if not message_queues[sock].empty():
                        next_msg = message_queues[sock].get_nowait()
                        sock.send(next_msg)
                    else:
                        # No more messages to send
                        outputs.remove(sock)
                except Exception as e:
                    status_message += f"Error writing to client {sock.getpeername()}: {e}\n"
                    outputs.remove(sock)
                    inputs.remove(sock)
                    del message_queues[sock]
                    sock.close()
            
            # Handle exceptional conditions
            for sock in exceptional:
                status_message += f"Exceptional condition on {sock.getpeername()}\n"
                if sock in outputs:
                    outputs.remove(sock)
                inputs.remove(sock)
                if sock in message_queues:
                    del message_queues[sock]
                sock.close()
                
    except Exception as e:
        status_message += f"Server error: {e}\n"
    finally:
        # Clean up
        for sock in inputs:
            if sock is not server_socket:
                sock.close()
        server_socket.close()
        
        # Calculate run duration
        duration = (datetime.now() - start_time).total_seconds()
        status_message += f"Server stopped after {duration:.2f} seconds.\n"
        
    return status_message

def task_func(file):
    # Check if file exists

        return []
    
    # Check if file is a CSV (simple check for .csv extension)

        return []

    base_name = os.path.basename(file)

                              capture_output=True, text=True)
        if result.returncode != 0:
            return []
    except Exception:
        return []
    
    # Get list of split files
    split_files = sorted(glob.glob(split_prefix + '*'))
    
    # Shuffle rows in each split file
    for split_file in split_files:
        try:
            # Read all rows
            with open(split_file, 'r', newline='', encoding='utf-8') as f:
                reader = csv.reader(f)
                rows = list(reader)
            
            # Shuffle rows
            random.shuffle(rows)
            
            # Write back to file
            with open(split_file, 'w', newline='', encoding='utf-8') as f:
                writer = csv.writer(f)
                writer.writerows(rows)

import os
import glob

# Constants
DIRECTORY = 'data'

def task_func(directory):
    result = []
    # Use glob to find all text files in the directory
    file_pattern = os.path.join(directory, "*.txt")
    text_files = glob.glob(file_pattern)
    
    for file_path in text_files:
        with open(file_path, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as file:
            content = file.read().strip()
            if not content:
                continue  # Skip empty files
            try:
                # Safely evaluate the string representation of dictionary
                dictionary = ast.literal_eval(content)
                if isinstance(dictionary, dict):

            writer = csv.DictWriter(csvfile, fieldnames=fieldnames)

            # Write the data rows
            writer.writerows(data)
    
    return file_path

from sklearn.feature_extraction.text import TfidfVectorizer
import re

def task_func(example_str):
    # Extract text not enclosed in square brackets
    cleaned_text = re.sub(r'\[.*?\]', '', example_str)
    # Remove extra whitespace
    cleaned_text = re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', cleaned_text).strip()
    
    # If no text remains after extraction, return empty dict
    if not cleaned_text:
        return {}
    
    # Use TfidfVectorizer to calculate TF-IDF scores
    vectorizer = TfidfVectorizer()
    tfidf_matrix = vectorizer.fit_transform([cleaned_text])

    tfidf_scores = tfidf_matrix.toarray()[0]

import json
import glob
def task_func(directory_path: str) -> list:
    if not os.path.exists(directory_path):
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"The directory {directory_path} does not exist.")
    
    json_files = glob.glob(os.path.join(directory_path, "*.json"))
    processed_files = []
    
    for file_path in json_files:
        try:
            with open(file_path, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as file:
                content = file.read()
            
            # Escape double quotes by prepending with double backslash
            escaped_content = re.sub(r'"', r'\\"', content)
            
            with open(file_path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as file:
                file.write(escaped_content)
            
            processed_files.append(file_path)
        except Exception as e:
            raise e
    
    return processed_files

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy.signal import get_window

def task_func(amplitude, frequency, time):
    # Generate the complex wave
    # Real part: amplitude * cos(2π * frequency * time)
    # Imaginary part: amplitude * sin(2π * frequency * time)
    complex_wave = amplitude * (np.cos(2 * np.pi * frequency * time) + 1j * np.sin(2 * np.pi * frequency * time))
    
    # Apply Hann window to reduce edge effects
    hann_window = get_window('hann', len(time))
    complex_wave = complex_wave * hann_window
    
    # Create the plot
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6))
    ax.plot(time, complex_wave.real, label='Real Part', color='blue')
    ax.plot(time, complex_wave.imag, label='Imaginary Part', color='red')
    ax.set_title("Complex Wave with Hann Window")
    ax.set_xlabel("Time")
    ax.set_ylabel("Amplitude")
    ax.legend()
    ax.grid(True)
    
    return complex_wave, fig, ax

import random
import math
def task_func(LETTERS=[chr(i) for i in range(97, 123)]):
    result = {}
    for letter in LETTERS:
        # Generate a random list of integers between 0 and 100 with length 1 to 10
        random_list = [random.randint(0, 100) for _ in range(random.randint(1, 10))]
        # Calculate the population standard deviation
        mean = sum(random_list) / len(random_list)
        variance = sum((x - mean) ** 2 for x in random_list) / len(random_list)
        std_dev = math.sqrt(variance)
        result[letter] = std_dev
    return result

The input dimension is determined based on the first feature set of X. - Compiles the model using binary cross-entropy loss and SGD optimizer. - Fits the model to the training data in a non-verbose mode. - Plots the Precision-Recall curve for the model based on the test set data.
Note that: Notes: The plot's x-axis is labeled 'Recall', and the y-axis is labeled 'Precision'. The title of the axes is set to 'Precision-Recall Curve'. The axes object allows for further customization of the plot outside the function.
The function should output with:
    keras.models.Sequential: The trained Keras model.
    matplotlib.axes._axes.Axes: The matplotlib Axes object for the Precision-Recall curve plot.
You should write self-contained code starting with:
```

from sklearn.metrics import precision_recall_curve
from tensorflow import keras

```

from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.metrics import precision_recall_curve
from tensorflow import keras
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

def task_func(X, Y):
    # Split the data into training (70%) and test (30%) sets
    X_train, X_test, Y_train, Y_test = train_test_split(X, Y, test_size=0.3, random_state=42)
    
    # Determine input dimension from the first feature set
    input_dim = X_train.shape[1]
    
    # Construct a Keras Sequential model with one hidden dense layer and sigmoid activation
    model = keras.Sequential([
        keras.layers.Dense(64, activation='sigmoid', input_shape=(input_dim,)),
        keras.layers.Dense(1, activation='sigmoid')
    ])
    
    # Compile the model using binary cross-entropy loss and SGD optimizer
    model.compile(loss='binary_crossentropy', optimizer='sgd', metrics=['accuracy'])
    
    # Fit the model to the training data in non-verbose mode
    model.fit(X_train, Y_train, epochs=50, batch_size=32, verbose=0)
    
    # Predict probabilities on the test set
    Y_pred_proba = model.predict(X_test).ravel()
    
    # Compute precision-recall curve
    precision, recall, _ = precision_recall_curve(Y_test, Y_pred_proba)
    
    # Create the Precision-Recall curve plot
    fig, ax = plt.subplots()
    ax.plot(recall, precision)
    ax.set_xlabel('Recall')
    ax.set_ylabel('Precision')
    ax.set_title('Precision-Recall Curve')
    
    return model, ax

def task_func(kwargs, target_dir="non_none_files"):
    copied_files = []
    target_path = Path(target_dir)
    target_path.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    
    for file_key, file_path in kwargs.items():
        file_path = Path(file_path)
        if file_path.exists() and file_path.is_file() and file_path.stat().st_size > 0:

            shutil.copy2(file_path, target_file)
            copied_files.append(str(target_file))

import os
import zipfile

TARGET_DIR = "downloaded_files"
TARGET_ZIP_FILE = "downloaded_files.zip"

def task_func(url):
    # Create target directory if it doesn't exist
    if not os.path.exists(TARGET_DIR):
        os.makedirs(TARGET_DIR)
    
    # Download the zip file
    urllib.request.urlretrieve(url, TARGET_ZIP_FILE)

import os
import glob
import zipfile

def task_func(directory):
    if not os.path.exists(directory):
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Directory {directory} not found.")
    
    # Get all files in the directory (not subdirectories)
    files = [f for f in glob.glob(os.path.join(directory, "*")) if os.path.isfile(f)]
    
    # If no files, return None
    if not files:
        return None
    
    # Define the zip file path
    zip_path = os.path.join(directory, "files.zip")
    
    # Create the zip file and add all files
    with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_path, 'w', zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as zipf:
        for file_path in files:
            # Add file to zip with just the filename (not the full path)
            zipf.write(file_path, os.path.basename(file_path))
    
    return zip_path

Decode a hexadecimal string from the 'q' query parameter of a URL. This function extracts the 'q' query parameter from the given URL, assumes it is a hexadecimal string, and decodes it into a UTF-8 string. If the hexadecimal string is invalid or cannot be decoded into a valid UTF-8 string, None is returned.
The function should output with:
    str or None: The decoded string if the 'q' parameter exists and is a valid hexadecimal, otherwise None.

import urllib.parse

```
output:
import binascii
import urllib.parse

def task_func(url):
    try:
        # Parse the URL and extract query parameters
        parsed_url = urllib.parse.urlparse(url)
        query_params = urllib.parse.parse_qs(parsed_url.query)
        
        # Check if 'q' parameter exists
        if 'q' not in query_params or not query_params['q']:
            return None
        
        # Get the value of 'q' parameter
        hex_string = query_params['q'][0]
        
        # Decode the hexadecimal string to bytes
        decoded_bytes = binascii.unhexlify(hex_string)
        
        # Convert bytes to UTF-8 string
        decoded_string = decoded_bytes.decode('utf-8')
        
        return decoded_string
    except (binascii.Error, UnicodeDecodeError, KeyError, IndexError):
        return None

def task_func(length, seed=None, alphabets=list(string.ascii_lowercase)):

        np.random.seed(seed)
    
    # Generate all possible strings of the given length from the alphabets
    all_strings = [''.join(p) for p in product(alphabets, repeat=length)]

import requests
import os
import zipfile

def task_func(url, destination_directory, headers=None):
    # Ensure the destination directory exists
    os.makedirs(destination_directory, exist_ok=True)
    
    # Download the zip file
    response = requests.get(url, headers=headers, stream=True)
    response.raise_for_status()
    
    # Define the path for the downloaded zip file
    zip_path = os.path.join(destination_directory, "downloaded_file.zip")
    
    # Save the downloaded content to a zip file
    with open(zip_path, 'wb') as f:
        for chunk in response.iter_content(chunk_size=8192):
            f.write(chunk)
    
    # Extract the contents of the zip file
    extracted_files = []
    with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_path, 'r') as zip_ref:
        zip_ref.extractall(destination_directory)
        extracted_files = zip_ref.namelist()
    
    # Remove the downloaded zip file after extraction
    os.remove(zip_path)
    
    return extracted_files

nltk.download('stopwords')

```

import re
import nltk
nltk.download('stopwords')
from nltk.corpus import stopwords
from collections import Counter
# Constants
STOPWORDS = set(stopwords.words('english'))
def task_func(text, n=2):
    # Convert to lowercase and remove non-alphanumeric characters
    text = re.sub(r'[^a-zA-Z\s]', '', text.lower())
    
    # Split into words
    words = text.split()
    
    # Remove stopwords and duplicates while preserving order
    filtered_words = []
    seen = set()
    for word in words:
        if word not in STOPWORDS and word not in seen:
            filtered_words.append(word)
            seen.add(word)
    
    # Generate n-grams
    ngrams = []
    for i in range(len(filtered_words) - n + 1):
        ngrams.append(' '.join(filtered_words[i:i + n]))
    
    # Count n-grams
    ngram_counts = Counter(ngrams)
    
    return dict(ngram_counts)

import hashlib
import binascii

def task_func(salt, cursor):
    if not isinstance(salt, str):
        raise TypeError("Salt must be a string")
    
    # Update passwords by hashing with SHA256 and the provided salt
    cursor.execute("SELECT id, password FROM users")
    users = cursor.fetchall()
    
    updated_count = 0
    for user_id, password in users:
        # Hash the password with SHA256 and the salt
        salted_password = password + salt
        hashed_password = hashlib.sha256(salted_password.encode('utf-8')).hexdigest()
        
        # Update the user's password in the database
        cursor.execute("UPDATE users SET password = ? WHERE id = ?", (hashed_password, user_id))
        updated_count += 1
    
    return updated_count

def task_func(N=100, CATEGORIES=["A", "B", "C", "D", "E"], seed=42):
    np.random.seed(seed)
    
    # Ensure each category appears at least once if N >= number of categories
    if N >= len(CATEGORIES):
        # Start with one instance of each category
        category_samples = CATEGORIES.copy()
        remaining = N - len(CATEGORIES)
        # Randomly sample the rest
        category_samples.extend(np.random.choice(CATEGORIES, size=remaining, replace=True))

    data_generator = ((x, np.sin(x), np.cos(x), abs(np.sin(x) - np.cos(x))) for x in x_values)

import numpy as np
import random

def task_func(MIN_WORDS, MAX_WORDS, WORDS_POOL):
    # Randomly choose the length of the sentence within the specified range
    sentence_length = random.randint(MIN_WORDS, MAX_WORDS)
    
    # Determine the number of words for the first half (including middle if odd)
    half_length = (sentence_length + 1) // 2
    
    # Randomly select words for the first half
    first_half = [random.choice(WORDS_POOL) for _ in range(half_length)]
    
    # Create the palindrome by mirroring the first half (excluding the middle word if odd)
    if sentence_length % 2 == 0:
        # Even length: mirror the entire first half
        second_half = first_half[::-1]
    else:
        # Odd length: mirror the first half excluding the last word
        second_half = first_half[-2::-1]
    
    # Combine the two halves to form the full palindrome sentence
    palindrome_words = first_half + second_half
    
    # Join the words into a sentence
    sentence = ' '.join(palindrome_words)
    
    # Verify the length is within the specified range
    assert MIN_WORDS <= len(sentence.split()) <= MAX_WORDS
    
    return sentence

import rsa
import os
import zipfile
from base64 import b64encode

def task_func(directory):
    # Generate RSA key pair
    (pubkey, privkey) = rsa.newkeys(2048)
    
    # Create a zip file to store encrypted files
    zip_filename = "encrypted_files.zip"
    
    with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_filename, 'w', zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as zipf:
        # Iterate through all files in the directory
        for root, dirs, files in os.walk(directory):
            for file in files:
                file_path = os.path.join(root, file)
                
                # Read the file data
                with open(file_path, 'rb') as f:
                    file_data = f.read()
                
                # Encrypt the file data with RSA public key
                # Note: RSA can only encrypt data up to key size minus padding
                # For 2048-bit RSA, max is ~245 bytes
                # So we need to split data into chunks
                chunk_size = 245
                encrypted_chunks = []
                
                for i in range(0, len(file_data), chunk_size):
                    chunk = file_data[i:i + chunk_size]
                    encrypted_chunk = rsa.encrypt(chunk, pubkey)
                    encrypted_chunks.append(encrypted_chunk)
                
                # Combine all encrypted chunks
                encrypted_data = b''.join(encrypted_chunks)
                
                # Save encrypted data to zip file with original filename
                arcname = os.path.relpath(file_path, directory)
                zipf.writestr(arcname, encrypted_data)
    
    return pubkey, zip_filename

import pandas as pd
from scipy.stats import pearsonr

def task_func(data):
    if len(data) < 2:
        return float('nan')
    
    # Convert scores from string to float
    scores = pd.to_numeric(data['scores'], errors='coerce')
    
    # Encode categorical grades into numerical values based on rank order
    grade_order = data['grades'].dropna().unique()
    grade_to_num = {grade: i for i, grade in enumerate(sorted(grade_order))}
    encoded_grades = data['grades'].map(grade_to_num)
    
    # Drop rows with NaN values in scores or encoded grades
    cleaned_data = pd.concat([scores, encoded_grades], axis=1).dropna()
    
    # Compute Pearson correlation coefficient
    correlation, _ = pearsonr(cleaned_data.iloc[:, 0], cleaned_data.iloc[:, 1])
    
    return correlation

# Importing the required libraries
import re
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.feature_extraction.text import CountVectorizer
from nltk.corpus import stopwords

def task_func(text, n=2):
    # Download stopwords if not already available
    try:
        stop_words = set(stopwords.words('english'))
    except LookupError:
        import nltk
        nltk.download('stopwords')
        stop_words = set(stopwords.words('english'))
    
    # Remove duplicate consecutive words
    words = re.split(r'\s+', text.strip())
    cleaned_words = []
    for i, word in enumerate(words):
        if i == 0 or word.lower() != cleaned_words[-1].lower():
            cleaned_words.append(word.lower())
    
    # Remove stopwords
    filtered_words = [word for word in cleaned_words if word not in stop_words]
    
    # Join words back into a string
    cleaned_text = ' '.join(filtered_words)
    
    # Create a CountVectorizer with n-gram range to capture co-occurrence
    vectorizer = CountVectorizer(ngram_range=(1, n), token_pattern=r'\b[a-zA-Z]+\b')
    X = vectorizer.fit_transform([cleaned_text])
    
    # Get feature names (words)
    feature_names = vectorizer.get_feature_names_out()
    
    # Create co-occurrence matrix
    # We'll use the dot product of the document-term matrix with its transpose
    co_occurrence_matrix = X.T.dot(X).toarray()
    
    # Create a DataFrame with the co-occurrence matrix
    df_co_occurrence = pd.DataFrame(co_occurrence_matrix, index=feature_names, columns=feature_names)
    
    # Plot the co-occurrence matrix
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 8))
    im = ax.imshow(co_occurrence_matrix, cmap='Blues', aspect='auto')
    
    # Set labels and title
    ax.set_xticks(np.arange(len(feature_names)))
    ax.set_yticks(np.arange(len(feature_names)))
    ax.set_xticklabels(feature_names, rotation=45, ha='right')
    ax.set_yticklabels(feature_names)
    ax.set_title('Co-occurrence Matrix of Words')
    
    # Add colorbar
    plt.colorbar(im, ax=ax)
    
    # Adjust layout to prevent label cutoff
    plt.tight_layout()
    
    return df_co_occurrence, ax

I can only unstack a block from on top of another block if the block I am unstacking was really on top of the other block.
I can only unstack a block from on top of another block if the block I am unstacking is clear.
Once I pick up or unstack a block, I am holding the block.
I can only put down a block that I am holding.
I can only stack a block on top of another block if I am holding the block being stacked.
I can only stack a block on top of another block if the block onto which I am stacking the block is clear.
Once I put down or stack a block, my hand becomes empty.
Once you stack a block on top of a second block, the second block is no longer clear.

---

def remove_first_last_char(s, char):
    if not s or char not in s:
        return s
    
    # Find first occurrence
    first_index = s.find(char)
    
    # Find last occurrence
    last_index = s.rfind(char)
    
    # Remove first occurrence
    s = s[:first_index] + s[first_index + 1:]
    
    # Remove last occurrence (adjust index if first and last are same)
    if first_index == last_index:
        return s
    else:
        s = s[:last_index - 1] + s[last_index:]
    
    return s
